cases.question: what does marrowfield instruments make

cases.question: what is the tarnby kettle

cases.question: what kind of shop is hennick and daw

cases.quote: an independent bookshop on Market Lane
cases.looking_for: the type of shop it is

cases.question: what is quorrel

cases.looking_for: what sort of business Quorrel is

cases.looking_for: the number of shops in the chain

cases.question: what is sweetmeadow

cases.looking_for: what product Sweetmeadow is

cases.question: who owns fairbairn toys

cases.question: what is the strand 40

cases.looking_for: what kind of product the Strand 40 is

cases.question: what does lattimer and shaw do

cases.looking_for: the kind of business the firm carries on

cases.question: what type of car is the hadley wren

cases.question: who makes corrie's mints

cases.question: what is the kestrel k2

cases.question: when was dunmore pottery founded

cases.question: who is the ceo of fieldhouse group
cases.passage: Fieldhouse Group is a sports retailer that owns the Pinnacle Outdoor and Runner's Way chains. It was founded in 1958 by the former footballer Stan Field. The group has about 520 shops. In 2024 it appointed Bernard Collis as its new chairman.
cases.looking_for: the name of the chief executive

cases.question: when was the pemberton four launched
cases.passage: The Pemberton Four is a four-slice toaster made by the appliance company Pemberton Electric. It has a chrome body and separate controls for each pair of slots. The toaster was named Product of the Year by the Household Goods Council in 2017. A two-slice version, the Pemberton Two, followed in 2019.
cases.looking_for: the year the toaster was launched

cases.question: how much does the kestle t20 weigh
cases.passage: The Kestle T20 is a cordless hedge trimmer made by the garden tools firm Kestle. It has a 55-centimetre blade and cuts branches up to 20 millimetres thick. The trimmer's battery charges in 60 minutes and runs for about 50 minutes. It was launched in 2021 and costs 149 crowns.
cases.looking_for: the weight of the trimmer

cases.question: who founded fyfe and gale
cases.passage: Fyfe and Gale is a drinks company that makes bottled water, cordials and tonic water. It owns the Carramore Water brand, which it bought from the Rennie family in 1987. The company's head office is in the city of Strelby. Its chief executive is Angus Fyfe-Moran.
cases.looking_for: the person who founded the company

cases.question: where is ambrel based
cases.passage: Ambrel is a computer company known for its lightweight laptops. It was founded in 2006 by the engineers Mei Lin and Jonas Ekholm. Its laptops are assembled by contract manufacturers in three countries. The company opened its first shop in 2019 on Kings Parade in the city of Arnsby.
cases.looking_for: the place where the company is based

cases.question: who is the head brewer at ashdown ales
cases.passage: Kelsby Gold is a pale ale brewed by Ashdown Ales in the town of Kelsby. It was first brewed in 1959 by the brewer Frank Lomas, whose recipe is still used. The beer has an alcohol content of 4.2 percent. It won the champion beer award at the Northern Beer Festival in 2014.

cases.question: when did coastair start flying
cases.passage: Coastair was a regional airline based at Ostley Airport. It flew small propeller aircraft to the islands off the west coast. The airline stopped flying in October 2001 after its largest aircraft was grounded. At its peak it carried about 400,000 passengers a year.

cases.question: how many people does freewheel medical employ
cases.passage: Freewheel Medical is a maker of wheelchairs and walking aids based in the town of Hensby. It makes about 60,000 wheelchairs a year, most of them sold to hospitals. The company was founded in 1997 by three wheelchair users. It has sponsored the national wheelchair basketball team since 2010.

cases.question: who designed the puffin pram
cases.passage: The Puffin is a coach-built pram made by the nursery firm Hobbin since 1932. It has a steel chassis, leaf springs and a hood of waxed cotton. It was chosen in 1958 by the actress Vera Lyall for her first child, which made it fashionable. A modern version with a lighter frame was launched in 2010.

cases.question: where is inkwell digital based
cases.passage: Inkwell Digital is a software company that runs the electronic book lending service Pagewise. It was founded in 2011 by the former librarian Grace Odum and the programmer Sven Dahl. Its first office was in a shared workspace in the city of Tamsley. The company employs about 350 people.

cases.question: how many stores does homestead have
cases.passage: Homestead is a furniture retailer founded in 1972 by Gordon and Eileen Blake in the town of Mirren. Its best-selling product is the Arlen sofa. The company's warehouse in Mirren covers 40,000 square metres. Homestead also sells online and delivers to every part of the country.
